BOL-6101.why: Harrowgate picked up and delivered it, its driver counted 12 cartons, and the delivery receipt notes 2 cartons crushed (Thursday 17 September 2026): good-order tender, damaged arrival and the amount make the prima facie case (Elmore & Stahl). 2 cartons of 4 Arden pendants at $172.50, $690 a carton, all broken: $1,380, full value, within 9 months of delivery. The receipt's notation is not itself a claim (49 CFR 370.3(c))

BOL-6087.why: Concealed damage: the receipt is clean, but a clean receipt is evidence, not a bar. Thistlewood's packing record shows the shade sets packed to spec (double-wall, foam corners) and Harrowgate's driver signed for 10 cartons in apparent good order; Brightwell found the damage two days after delivery, reported it to Harrowgate within its 5 business days, and Harrowgate's own inspector found forklift-tine punctures at fork height. 3 Calla shade sets at $390: $1,170

BOL-6122.why: Damage noted at delivery and confirmed by Harrowgate's inspector, but Rosa signed the released-value declaration for Harrowgate's released rate: liability is limited to $2.00 a pound (49 U.S.C. 14706(c)(1)(A); Rules Tariff HGF-100 item 780), and the crate weighed 85 lb. The claim is for $170, not the chandelier's $2,600 invoice price

traps.BOL-5950: Delivered Friday 12 December 2025, one carton short; the shortage was only noted on the receipt, which is not a claim (370.3(c)), and Harrowgate's 9 months after delivery ran out on 12 September 2026. A claim filed now is out of time
traps.BOL-6064: The shipper's own act: Thistlewood's packer shipped the sconces below its own spec, in single-wall cartons with no padding, and Harrowgate's inspector found the cartons undamaged outside and the breakage from movement inside. The carrier is not liable for damage the shipper's packing caused
traps.BOL-5822: Already claimed: HC-30551 was filed on 2 June 2026 and is under investigation; a second claim for the same bill of lading duplicates it
traps.BOL-6115: Sablecroft Transport picked up, carried and delivered this shipment alone; Harrowgate never had it and is not liable for it. The wet cartons are claimed against Sablecroft, by mail

BOL-5871.why: The whole pallet, picked up Monday 12 January 2026, was never delivered, and Larkfield closed the trace 'unable to locate'. A trace is not a claim (370.3(c)), and Larkfield's terms give 9 months after the bill of lading date for a shipment never delivered: Monday 12 October 2026, three days away. 8 cartons at $407.50: $3,260, with Pellham's statement of non-receipt (370.7(c))
